summary: Mobility is stabilising at a near‑normal MF‑Index of 71, but actual fuel savings remain far below theoretical expectations and high‑risk sectors continue to drive travel. Public transport ridership is recovering to about 86% of pre‑pandemic levels, offering a lever for further modal shift if supported by policy.

signals.detail: While the modelled ceiling suggests 35.7 M L saved per week, only 334 k L were recorded in the first week of the mandate—a 1% realization rate—indicating weak compliance and limited immediate environmental benefit.
Daily PT trips total 1.24 M, roughly 86% of the 2019 pre‑pandemic daily average, showing a modest rebound but still 14% below historic levels, suggesting room for targeted demand‑generation measures.

Retail, logistics and construction sectors exhibit mobility scores above 90 with WFH rates under 15%, signalling high exposure to congestion and fuel cost volatility that could dampen post‑pandemic economic recovery.
WFH adoption is uneven: public/GLC employees at 60% versus logistics and construction below 10%, creating equity gaps and limiting the overall effectiveness of the remote‑work mandate.
Elevated fuel prices (RON95 RM4.27/L) provide an incentive for modal shift, yet the modest PT ridership recovery and low fuel‑saving compliance suggest the shift is not yet materialising at scale.

recommendation: Introduce sector‑specific WFH incentives for logistics, retail and construction to raise remote work rates to at least 25% by Q4 2027, coupled with a targeted fuel‑efficiency rebate for fleets that achieve 10% weekly fuel‑saving benchmarks. Simultaneously, invest in PT service frequency and fare subsidies to push daily ridership above 1.3 M trips within six months, supporting a durable modal shift.
